statement: Arbitrary-coefficient generic kernels are detected integrally by hyperelementary restrictions; p-locally by p-hyperelementary restrictions; cyclic restriction-zero classes are killed by |G|²
depends_on: Dress1973 Proposition5.2 pp210–212; Swan Green action rechecked
notes: Sufficient subgroup vanishing gate only; tame cyclic tests are ordinary finite-etale commutative K0 comparisons; no coefficient-localization or etale K0-descent assumption

statement: Injectivity of every cyclic or hyperelementary generic comparison is not necessary for the symmetric-group polynomial theorem: k=Z and C23
depends_on: C:DVR; Koeck1998 Example6.9(d); explicit ideal class of order3 in Q(sqrt(-23))
notes: Symmetric-group kernels vanish over Z while C23 has a nonzero cyclotomic ideal-class kernel; subgroup classes need not induce nontrivially
